surface: SUNNYVAiLE LIBRAiRY / Who’s Who in AI

readerContract.humanQuestion: Which organisations and people actually shape AI, what do they control, and how are they connected?
readerContract.promisedPayoff: The reader can locate a company, lab, product, supplier, funder or regulator on a layered map and read a relationship without confusing investment, ownership, hosting or distribution.
readerContract.priorKnowledge: No technical or business background is assumed.
readerContract.centralMentalModel: AI is a dependency stack: labs depend on compute, chips depend on a supply chain, products depend on distribution, alliances move money and capacity, and public bodies set or enforce rules.
readerContract.dailyLifeConnection: The map helps readers understand who is behind a tool they use, why a partnership matters, and which announcement could change availability, price, privacy or power.
readerContract.surfaceJob: A living global dependency atlas and practical Who’s Who, not a ranking, celebrity list or product directory.
readerContract.desiredFeeling: I can see who does what, who depends on whom, and what changed when the news names a new deal.

canonicalTruth.freshnessTrigger: Any change to the book job or catalogue boundary.
Before every review and on any material relationship change.
Any change to active reference-content requirements.
Any change to organisations, people and power ownership boundaries.
Any change to LAiDIES voice or public-copy rules.
Any change to the conversational, Hannah Fry or Feynman-style comprehension gate.

strengthsToUse: Separate current fact, relationship and uncertainty.
patternsNotToCopy: Do not repeat the FAQ scaffold.
Do not turn profiles into isolated answers.

glossaryAccumulation.producerGuard: Entities sit in a dependency map rather than an alphabetical name pile.
glossaryAccumulation.preventionEvidence: The layer map and relationship verbs provide structure.

templateRepetition.producerGuard: Profile cards stay compact while layer chapters use maps, comparisons and cases.
templateRepetition.preventionEvidence: The format varies by reader job.

decorativeAnalogy.producerGuard: The supply-chain map is literal, not a decorative analogy.

referenceConfetti.producerGuard: A named person or company appears only for a sourced control point.
referenceConfetti.preventionEvidence: The inclusion rule rejects fame alone.

missingMechanism.producerGuard: Every relationship names what moves between parties and what control follows.

genericAction.producerGuard: The reader redraws one announcement as a sourced relationship statement.
genericAction.preventionEvidence: The useful action produces a relationship receipt.

jargonBeforeMeaning.producerGuard: Explain the ordinary confusion before terms such as foundry or lithography.
jargonBeforeMeaning.preventionEvidence: The opening begins with company-product confusion.

disconnectedSystem.producerGuard: Every profile belongs to a layer and connects to another dependency.
disconnectedSystem.preventionEvidence: The stack is the shared spine.

joylessInstruction.producerGuard: Use consequential current relationships and plain stakes.
joylessInstruction.preventionEvidence: The Microsoft-OpenAI-Azure case exposes a confusion readers encounter.

purposeTooNarrow.producerGuard: No single US lab or chatbot defines the map.
purposeTooNarrow.preventionEvidence: The architecture includes global labs, supply chain and public power.

mechanismBeforeMotivation.producerGuard: Begin with why the distinction changes what readers believe.
mechanismBeforeMotivation.preventionEvidence: The opening asks whether an investor owns the lab.

workedExampleOvertakesBookPurpose.producerGuard: The OpenAI relationship teaches the reading method and then transfers to chips and regulation.
workedExampleOvertakesBookPurpose.preventionEvidence: Worked and transfer cases occupy different layers.

technicalExplainerVoice.producerGuard: Write as a candid guide to power and dependence, not a corporate database.
technicalExplainerVoice.preventionEvidence: The payoff is reader orientation and judgment.

draftArchitecture.plainAnswer: There is no single AI industry: model labs, products, clouds, chips, factories, data platforms, investors and regulators form a dependency stack, and the power becomes clearer when every connection is named with a verb.
causalSequence: Begin with one ordinary chatbot request and reveal each organisation needed to make or deliver the answer.
Identify each entity type only after its job is visible.
Name what it controls and what it depends on in ordinary language.
Label each relationship with a precise verb and explain that verb through a familiar example.
Separate announced commitments from delivered facts.
Let the reader redraw an unseen headline and diagnose any missing relationship.
draftArchitecture.workedCase: Follow one ordinary chatbot request from product to model lab, cloud capacity, chip designer, foundry, memory and public rules; then translate the OpenAI-Microsoft-Azure agreement without calling Microsoft the owner of OpenAI.
draftArchitecture.transferCase: Trace a different announcement through the same stack and distinguish investor, owner, supplier, host, distributor and regulator without copying the book’s vocabulary.
draftArchitecture.usefulAction: Take one AI headline and explain to a colleague who gives whom what, what changes, and what the announcement does not prove.

analogyPlan.analogy: A restaurant meal reaches the table through the dining room, kitchen, ingredients, equipment, building and health rules.
analogyPlan.mapping: Product, model lab, cloud, chips, manufacturing inputs and public rules each perform a different necessary job.
analogyPlan.limit: AI supply relationships are not a restaurant hierarchy and one company may occupy several layers.
analogyPlan.whyItHelps: It lets the reader see dependence before learning industry vocabulary.

humourPlan.lessonJob: Use restrained wit about corporate family-tree confusion; never let the joke replace a legal or ownership distinction.

draftArchitecture.formatSpecificStructure: Begin with one answer’s journey, then use that familiar route to introduce organisation, model, product, cloud, chips, factories, data, money, public power and decision-makers. Profiles answer why the reader should remember the entity. Finish with an unseen-headline teach-back and dated change log.
draftArchitecture.antiTemplateDecision: Use natural mini-stories and relationship diagrams before compact lookup cards. Define equity, hosting, foundry and lithography in ordinary language at first use; do not produce a wall of corporate entries.

communicationDesign.surfaceAdaptation: Use a scannable reference whose maps and cases begin with ordinary confusion and expose invisible dependencies. Never imitate a presenter or Hannah Fry’s voice.

humanQuestion.reason: Readers see overlapping company, model and product names.
humanQuestion.plannedEvidence: Open with the difference between a lab, a product, an investor and a cloud provider.

usefulCuriosity.reason: A familiar chatbot depends on companies readers rarely see.
usefulCuriosity.plannedEvidence: Ask what must exist behind one answer before revealing the stack.

invisibleProcessConcrete.reason: Funding, hosting, fabrication and licensing are invisible in the interface.
invisibleProcessConcrete.plannedEvidence: Use named arrows and dated relationship cases.

familiarTechnicalMovement.reason: Supply-chain terms matter only after the reader sees their consequence.
familiarTechnicalMovement.plannedEvidence: Move from a chatbot to cloud, accelerator, foundry, memory and lithography in plain language.

limitationsConsequences.reason: Corporate announcements are easy to overread.
limitationsConsequences.plannedEvidence: Label company-reported commitments, delivered facts and unknowns separately.

humourSurprise.reason: Light wit can clarify that investment is not ownership.
humourSurprise.plannedEvidence: Use one earned line, not a comic corporate genealogy.

betterNextQuestion.reason: The map must survive new deals.
betterNextQuestion.plannedEvidence: End each relationship case with what changed and what must be rechecked.

explanationArc.adaptation: Layer introductions use the full movement; compact profile cards retain only the distinctions needed for lookup.

representativeProofPlan.highestRisk: The book could become US-centric, stale, promotional or confuse investment with control.
representativeProofPlan.plannedProof: Draft the complete opening and the OpenAI-Microsoft-Azure relationship, then transfer the method to ASML and EU public power with dated primary sources.
representativeProofPlan.acceptanceOutcome: A cold reader can distinguish company, product, cloud, investor, supplier and regulator and accurately restate one relationship.
